title: Backup transport foundation: implement the send-all contract
value: Give the backup client and server one real, reusable byte-transport primitive instead of a success-reporting no-op. This is the implementation portion of the still-open November 12 proposal.
why_now: Catch-up for November 13, actually reviewed and published on November 16. Sources describe their current commits, not a review performed on the missed date. The current header and stub confirm the same unfinished send-all task. Compared with the numerical wrapper and scheduler CLI, this directly unlocks protocol and file-transfer work with a narrow observable contract. Carrying it forward avoids inventing completed work or unrelated novelty. The next two catch-up packets elaborate verification and a dependent protocol layer; neither is assumed finished. This review inspected sources, tests and CI configuration; it did not execute the C, scheduler or numerical suites.
effort: About 1-2 hours for the primitive and basic socket test on Linux/WSL; robust failure coverage is a separate dependent packet.
steps: Implement only network_send_all, retaining the existing public return convention. Send from a byte pointer advanced by the number actually written; do not assume one send call transfers the full buffer.

Handle EINTR without losing progress; treat permanent errors and zero-progress sends as failures rather than success or an infinite loop. Document the blocking-socket assumption and the policy for EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK; do not busy-spin.

Define zero-length and invalid-argument behavior, including null data with nonzero count. Use a portable, documented approach to prevent SIGPIPE from terminating the process when the peer disconnects.
Add one genuine socketpair transfer test with an independent receiver and binary payload. Keep listener, connection, receive and formatted-line stubs explicitly outside the completion claim.
acceptance_checks: An independent socketpair receiver gets the exact bytes and length, including embedded zero bytes, and the sender reports success only after transferring the complete payload.
Zero-length and invalid-argument cases match the documented policy; a zero-progress or permanent send failure terminates with the error convention.
A disconnected peer does not cause false success or unexpected SIGPIPE termination. Other networking functions are still documented as unfinished.
Run the project build and focused network test on a supported POSIX environment; record actual results separately from this proposal.

evidence.observation: Reviewed November 16: src is explicitly described as implementation skeletons and stubs; the README documents reliable byte framing, Linux/macOS builds, and make test.
Reviewed November 16: network_send_all must loop until count bytes are transferred; network_send_line must format a text line and append a newline. Both return zero on success and minus one on error.
Reviewed November 16: both send functions ignore their arguments and unconditionally return zero. The file includes stdarg.h but network_send_line does not format or send anything.
Reviewed November 16: the only checks initialize recv_buf_t and assert zero length/start. No socket is created and neither send function is exercised.
Reviewed November 16: tests/test_% links common sources and lock_table.c with pthread flags; make test discovers test_*.c binaries and stops when a test returns failure.

Reviewed November 16: Ubuntu CI installs build dependencies, runs a canary check, builds with make all, then invokes make test. This is workflow configuration, not evidence that CI passed in this review.

Current source inspected November 16 converts W and unpacks its shape without explicit channel validation. Its README documents assumed-valid matrices; the separately inspected tests cover valid analytic channels, not a custom-input CLI.

Current main inspected November 16 uses Processes.txt, a fixed quantum of 10, and unconditional chart generation. The README confirms a file-driven interactive workflow, so a configurable headless runner remains useful.

alternatives.title: Build the outstanding validated custom-channel runner
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Impact: lets numerical users supply safe custom inputs. Effort: roughly 2-4 hours. Evidence is strong from the README, solver and numerical tests; however, this repeats the existing channel-runner backlog while the backup transport currently reports success without transferring data. No completion of that earlier proposal is assumed.

alternatives.title: Expose input selection and a headless metrics mode
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Impact: easier reproducible classroom runs. Effort: roughly 2-4 hours plus checking expected scheduling outputs. The entry-point limitation is confirmed, but output correctness needs further behavioral verification. The backup networking contracts give a smaller, more direct implementation and test boundary.
